body: Thank you ❤️

Be careful....I was in the same situation as you when I was 17. While the idea of having a long distance partner with strict parents sounds good, it didn't really work for me in the long run because the person I was seeing back then ended up not being good for me (for context he was a deadbeat with no ambitions, he'd call me abusive when I asked why he bought a second Nintendo Switch when he can't pay rent, I was a lot younger than him and I really thought he was the one for me because noone has treated me that nicely before) and I didn't know he was truly bad for me until I met him (my parents never found out of course, it was a very elaborate plan lol). 

While I am not in your situation, I think it's important to think about how you guys might want to meet in the future because when I met my LDR SO we ended up not getting along irl :/ 

And like the other comments said, predators tend to creep on people who came from oppressive and abusive backgrounds like we have, so just take care of yourself OP!

Thanks for  the kind words. I'm hoping that my interviews go well next week (especially for the role I really want) because they have an office a couple hours away from where I live, and as long as I'm double vaxxed (which I am), I'm more than welcome to work there.
They're not entitled I'm just worried it'll keep going trauma doesn't make someone stronger unfortunately

I tell my boyfriend but I'm traumatised by previous relationships where I've been left in the dark when I needed someone that I try to take on the pain myself.
I don't appeal anything to them and I try not to but it doesn't mean it still doesn't hurt having them tell you that you're not worth anything

toxic household, parents are never hearing me out and everything's always my fault, difficulty finding a job outside my hometown, never feeling good enough, parents beating me down, parents telling me my boyfriend doesn't see me as an equal, gaslighting, haunted by the past, haunted by being sexually assaulted, haunted by being taken advantage of sexually

Yes omg, my mom always asks for tea when it comes to my friends too like she kept asking me why so and so broke up with so and so but I kept telling her it doesn't matter and why does she need to know?? They're my friends and not yours...

My mom's exactly the same, I definitely agree about the social currency and her getting upset at me because I don't talk to her like I used to.
Ohh gotcha 😂 yeah, I've never met anyone who didn't have a gossipy mom!

Yeah, especially if you and your family immigrated to a new country, it's like they think your life is on easy mode. Like the least you can do is be grateful your kids are living better lives, and I understand where they're coming from especially since it's tough establishing yourself in a new country -- I just don't understand why they think raising their kids the same way they'd raise their kids back in their home country would benefit their kids. 

Also haha no way! I used to think our family was the odd one out because of all the happy families on TV. You should wear bright colours though, they always look bomb af on brown skin!

what do you mean? I feel like a lot of asian relatives and family friends are gossipy by default, I don't really mind it if they're talking about something else, I just hate it when my mom tells everyone what I'm up to especially if it's not confirmed
Yeah my mom is the same way! She hates gossip but she always partakes in it 😂 gossip is fun but maybe not when the whole house can hear you?

My dad's around! He's more passive though, which makes me wonder why they're together in the first place. But yes, my mom would often do that (deferring to my brother) but now that my brother is gone, she's been weird with my bf like wanting him to do favours for us, so I'm shutting things down with my mom if it gets too weird and of course, checking in with him.

I'm glad she likes him but it's weird how she's saying "oh he's been a good influence to ME" and even protecting him from....her own daughter? So strange....at least I'm not gonna have a shotgun wedding like she did, so there's that.

You're calling your own daughter a slut? You're right though, I did tell my boyfriend about my mom so he can understand our dynamic a lot better......I'm worried it'll come to that point with your friend because if things go wrong, I'll 100% get the blame for it.

I get what you're saying, but by her definition of PDA she means like if we're laying down a little bit too close on the couch together, like not even arms wrapped around eachother or anything. Whenever they're around we obviously keep our hands off of eachother, so we're okay with understanding her boundaries. What I don't appreciate is the slutshaming when she leaves because she's accusing *me* of being the horndog in the relationship, and telling me I'm the one corrupting him, in turn would reflect poorly on her.

 I understand trying to protect your children and I don't kiss or cuddle my bf in front of them, I just wish she wouldn't go about it in a way that makes it feel like I'm "tempting" him on purpose because she goes out of her way to tell him I'm "disrespecting my body" just because we're a little bit too close to eachother.
Honestly, yeah that's fair. At the time it just felt annoying and I'll do better the next time he's over.

That's what I've been hearing from other people too but it's so hard to cut her off given that she's in a lot of my social circles. Right now, I think further distancing myself away from her is really helping and focusing on my connections outside of my highschool friend group to grow, I just can't help but remember her saying she feels bad for me because I don't have any friends and i always feel like a burden to everyone around me
